title: Bright Angel Trail: Rim to River
map_label: 3D view of the Grand Canyon following the hiker down the Bright Angel Trail to the Colorado River

stops.alt: Layered red cliffs of the Grand Canyon glowing in the last light of the day
stops.title: The edge of the canyon
stops.text: You start on the rim, with the whole canyon below you. The trail drops {gain} to the Colorado River, and every step down is a step back up.

winter.text: The rim sits at about 2,100 m (6,900 ft), so it gets real winter: snow and ice can lie on the first part of the trail even when the river is warm. Many hikers carry traction on the upper trail in winter.

stops.commons_file: Grand Canyon National Park, Sunset From Bright Angel Trail 3379 - Flickr - Grand Canyon NPS.jpg
stops.alt: Red and orange buttes glowing at sunset under a dramatic sky, seen from the Bright Angel Trail
stops.title: Buttes at sunset
stops.text: Across the canyon, each butte and ridge glows a different shade of red as the sun drops.

winter.title: Buttes above the snow
winter.text: Across the canyon, each butte and ridge shows a different shade of red. In winter, snow and ice can linger on the upper trail.

stops.commons_file: 408 Bright Angel Trail - Grand Canyon - Jacob's Ladder (4753750420).jpg
stops.alt: Switchbacks of Jacob's Ladder cut into the canyon wall
stops.title: Jacob's Ladder
stops.text: Tight switchbacks cut into the canyon wall, one of the best-known landmarks of the trail.

winter.text: The long switchbacks below the rim are the part that holds snow and ice in winter. Go slowly: it is steep, and everything you descend you have to climb back.

stops.alt: The stone 3-Mile Resthouse on the Bright Angel Trail below the rim
stops.title: The second resthouse
stops.text: Another stone shelter with seasonal water. Indian Garden is still ahead, and so is the climb back.

stops.alt: A rocky butte rising from the inner canyon under a hazy sky
stops.title: Buttes above the trail
stops.text: Down here the buttes rise above you, and the rim is far overhead.

stops.commons_file: Grand Canyon National Park Indian Garden 3511 (6063712657).jpg
stops.alt: A shaded shelter among green trees at Indian Garden, with red cliffs behind
stops.title: Indian Garden
stops.text: Green cottonwoods in the middle of the desert, in the oasis NPS now calls Havasupai Gardens. The river is still about 3 miles ahead.

stops.commons_file: Grand Canyon NP- Bright Angel Trail - Devil's Corkscrew 50247 (52028292714).jpg
stops.alt: Switchbacks of Devil's Corkscrew dropping into the inner gorge below Indian Garden
stops.title: Devil's Corkscrew
stops.text: Below Indian Garden the trail zigzags down steep switchbacks into the dark rock of the inner gorge, and the river is almost in reach.

stops.commons_file: Colorado River from Above - Flickr - brewbooks (1).jpg
stops.alt: The Colorado River far below, with the Silver Bridge crossing it
stops.title: The Colorado River
stops.text: The trail reaches the river at {elev}, about {gain} below where you started. The Silver Bridge is just ahead.

summer.text: In summer the inner canyon is far hotter than the rim, and heat is the main danger on this trail. The park advises against hiking to the river and back in a day in summer.

stops.commons_file: Colorado River near sunset - Flickr - brewbooks.jpg
stops.alt: The Colorado River between steep red canyon walls
stops.title: Beside the river
stops.text: For the next stretch the trail follows the river bank, between the water and the walls of the inner gorge.

stops.commons_file: Grand Canyon National Park - Silver Bridge 1277 (50545174893).jpg
stops.alt: The Silver Bridge suspension footbridge over the Colorado River
stops.title: Crossing the Colorado
stops.text: The Silver Bridge, also called the Bright Angel Suspension Bridge, carries you over the Colorado River to the north side.

stops.alt: Cottonwood trees beside Bright Angel Creek at Bright Angel Campground
stops.title: Bright Angel Creek
stops.text: Cottonwoods shade the creek at the campground, a cool, green stop at the bottom of the canyon.

stops.alt: Stone cabins and cottonwood trees at Phantom Ranch
stops.title: Phantom Ranch
stops.text: About {gain} below the rim, at the stone cabins of Phantom Ranch, the lodge at the bottom of the canyon.

summer.text: Down here it is the hottest place on the trail in summer, with air temperatures far above the rim's. Rest in the shade and carry plenty of water and salty food.

seasons.note: Season view is illustrative: snow and colour are drawn on the map, not measured. The photos are real.
